End-point loss of an HP-type filter

Source: R/diagnostics.R
hp_loss.Rd

hp_loss() measures the end-point bias of a filter by the loss of Bloechl (2014) used by Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017): for every time \(t\), the squared distance of the gain of its estimate from the gain at the centre of the series. The loss is zero in the middle and grows towards the ends; the fully modified HP filter chooses its end-point weights to make the total small.

Usage

hp_loss(
  x,
  lambda = 1600,
  form = c("rows", "differences"),
  theta = seq(0, 3.1, 0.1),
  weight = 0.1
)

# Default S3 method
hp_loss(
  x,
  lambda = 1600,
  form = c("rows", "differences"),
  theta = seq(0, 3.1, 0.1),
  weight = 0.1
)

Arguments

x

the length \(T\) of a series, or a result of hp_filter(), mhp_filter() or fmhp_filter() (with as_dt = FALSE).

lambda

a smoothing parameter, or one per observation (form = "rows") or per second difference (form = "differences"); ignored for a result.

form

"rows" (default) or "differences"; see fmhp_filter().

theta

the frequencies (default \(0, 0.1, \dots, 3.1\)).

weight

the factor \(\theta\) (default 0.1).

Value

An object of class c("mhp_loss", "mhp_result", "list"): loss (a data.table with t and loss), total (\(L\)), lambda_t, form. plot() draws \(l(t)\) against \(t\) (Figures 3 and 3b of the paper).

Details

$$l(t) = \theta\sum_{\omega}\left[P_c(\omega) - P_t(\omega)\right]^2, \qquad L = \sum_{t=1}^{T} l(t),$$ with the gains \(P_t\) of hp_gain(), \(\omega = 0, 0.1, \dots, 3.1\), \(\theta = 0.1\) (their spacing) and \(c = \mathrm{round}(T/2)\) (Hanif et al. 2017, eqs. 7 and 8, and their MATLAB code). The loss depends on \(T\) and the smoothing parameters only, not on the data: for the HP filter with \(\lambda = 100\) it is 1.731 to 1.735 for 41 to 55 observations, the values of Table 3a of the paper.

References

Bloechl, A. (2014). Reducing the excess variability of the Hodrick-Prescott filter by flexible penalization. Discussion Paper 2014-1, University of Munich.

Hanif, M. N., Iqbal, J. and Choudhary, M. A. (2017). Fully modified HP filter. SBP Working Paper Series, No. 88, State Bank of Pakistan.

See also

fmhp_filter, hp_gain, fmhp_compare

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

hl <-
  hp_loss(
      x      = 55
    , lambda = 100
    , form   = "rows"
    , theta  = seq(from = 0, to = 3.1, by = 0.1)
    , weight = 0.1
    )
hl$total
#> [1] 1.734501
plot(x = hl)
